title: Oracle threshold sweep: per-document oracle at attribution-cos 0.90→0.60 vs matched per-document random, plus dense f488/f976
result: No: the attribution oracle is not a better per-document selector than uniform random at matched keep, and it loses below 0.85. 1,952 rows/task, single cut @7, eval_size 500/cell, no-cot, 1 seed each (seed noise ~±0.03 on the 8k mean: random 17.7% vs 19.7% differ by .028). 8k mean: ~18% keep oracle 0.90 .824 vs random .813 (17.7%) / .841 (19.7%), a tie; ~12% keep oracle 0.80 .721 vs random .796 (11.7%), outlier .409 vs .740; 0.85 .837 (13.1%); 0.70 .648 / 0.60 .643 sit at dense f488 (.667) cost-for-cost (FTM <=1.34x/<=1.47x). Best oracle FTM 4.16x (0.85) vs recipe 4.60x. Per-doc allocation = no empty docs and gold share = body share for both; the oracle differs only by piling picks on each document's first tokens (outlier first-8-token share 27% at 0.90 → 71% at 0.60, uniform 5%), and its routed train CE drops far below dense (0.80: .152 vs .211). Per-row 0.90 + random x1.15: total keep 34.8% (oracle 16.2%), gold keep .774 vs distractor .334, routed CE .106 vs dense .184, 8k .733 (outlier .408): random tokens do not fix the per-row leak. 0.90/0.80 re-scored on the local path (same as random): within 0.004/cell of Lambda.
